name: fix_csharp_modify_during_foreach
description: Fixes a List mutated during foreach (throws InvalidOperationException) to remove in place correctly
prompts: Pruner.RemoveEvens(List<int> items) in Pruner.cs should remove every even number from the list and return it. It's broken: it calls items.Remove(x) INSIDE a `foreach (var x in items)`, and mutating a List while enumerating it throws InvalidOperationException ('Collection was modified'). Fix RemoveEvens to remove all even numbers correctly (e.g. List<T>.RemoveAll, or iterate a snapshot), returning the same list instance behavior: only the odd numbers remain, in their original order. Keep the class name and the RemoveEvens(List<int>) signature.

setup_files.app.csproj:
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- tests/ has its own project; without this the SDK's default glob
         compiles tests/*.cs into the app itself, where xunit isn't referenced -->
    <Compile Remove="tests/**" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>
